title: DiffusionDet: Diffusion Model for Object Detection
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)

problem.summary: Modern detectors regress and classify on hand-designed object candidates (sliding windows, proposals, anchors, reference points), and even DETR-style models depend on a fixed set of learnable queries; no prior method lets detection start from arbitrary random boxes, vary the number of evaluation boxes, or reuse the detection head iteratively across sparse and crowded scenes.
statements: Most detectors define surrogate regression and classification on empirically designed object candidates such as windows, proposals, anchors and reference points.
Query-based detectors still depend on a fixed set of learnable object queries.
Prior detectors couple the number of processed boxes between training and evaluation and use their heads only once per forward pass.

evidence.quote: the majority of detectors solve detection tasks by defining surrogate regression and classification on empirically designed object candidates, such as sliding windows [28, 80], region proposals [27, 74], anchor boxes [56, 72] and reference points [19, 106, 113].
While these works achieve a simple and effective design, they still have a dependency on a fixed set of learnable queries.
A natural question is: is there a simpler approach that does not even need the surrogate of learnable queries?

background.summary: DiffusionDet builds on two lines: query-based end-to-end detection (DETR, Sparse R-CNN, Deformable DETR), whose decoders it borrows, and denoising diffusion generative models, which had been applied to segmentation and generation but, as the paper claims, never successfully to object detection.

relatedWork.name: DETR
relatedWork.relation: prior end-to-end detector that replaced hand-designed candidates with learnable queries
relatedWork.quote: Recently, DETR [10] proposes learnable object queries to eliminate the hand-designed components and set up an end-to-end detection pipeline

relatedWork.name: Sparse R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: source of the 6-stage detection decoder, but with fixed learned proposals instead of random boxes
relatedWork.quote: DiffusionDet begins from random boxes while Sparse R-CNN uses a fixed set of learned boxes in inference

relatedWork.name: Diffusion models
relatedWork.relation: generative paradigm recast as the noise-to-box detection mechanism
relatedWork.quote: Diffusion models have achieved great success in many generation tasks [3, 4, 40, 71, 95] and start to be explored in perception tasks like image segmentation [1, 5, 6, 13, 31, 47, 98].

relatedWork.name: Diffusion for segmentation (Bit Diffusion)
relatedWork.relation: closest prior use of diffusion for perception, but not detection
relatedWork.quote: Chen et al. [13] adopted Bit Diffusion model [14] for panoptic segmentation [49] of images and videos.

evidence.quote: However, despite significant interest in this idea, there are no previous solutions that successfully adapt generative diffusion models for object detection
To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work that adopts a diffusion model for object detection.

solution.summary: DiffusionDet formulates detection as denoising diffusion over box coordinates: training pads and noises ground-truth boxes and learns to reverse the process with a set prediction loss, while inference starts from random Gaussian boxes and progressively refines them with DDIM steps and box renewal; a single-run image encoder feeds a 6-stage Sparse R-CNN-style decoder that is reused across steps, giving dynamic box counts and iterative evaluation with shared parameters.
solution.approach: Cast object detection as a generative denoising process from noisy boxes to object boxes, refined iteratively at inference by a reusable detection decoder conditioned on once-computed image features.
components: forward diffusion corrupting padded ground-truth boxes with scheduled Gaussian noise
image encoder (ResNet or Swin with FPN) executed once per image
6-stage detection decoder cropping RoI features from the feature map
set prediction loss with optimal-transport top-k assignment
DDIM sampling to step boxes between timesteps at inference
box renewal replacing low-scoring predictions with fresh random boxes
timestep embedding so one head serves all sampling steps

evidence.quote: We propose DiffusionDet, a new framework that formulates object detection as a denoising diffusion process from noisy boxes to object boxes.
During training, we first construct the diffusion process from ground-truth boxes to noisy boxes and then train the model to reverse this process.
The inference procedure of DiffusionDet is a denoising sampling process from noise to object boxes.
we propose to separate the whole model into two parts, image encoder and detection decoder
We apply set prediction loss [10, 91, 115] on the set of Ntrain predictions.

experiments.summary: DiffusionDet is trained on COCO and evaluated on COCO val, zero-shot transferred from COCO to CrowdHuman, fully tuned on CrowdHuman, and benchmarked on LVIS v1.0; ablations study padding strategies, signal scaling, numbers of boxes and sampling steps, box renewal and running time, against Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, Cascade R-CNN, DETR, Deformable DETR and Sparse R-CNN.

benchmarks.split: val, extra evaluation boxes/steps over 29.4 baseline

evidence.quote: DiffusionDet achieves 5.3 AP and 4.8 AP gains when evaluated with more boxes and iteration steps, under a zero-shot transfer setting from COCO to CrowdHuman.

With ResNet-50 [37] backbone, DiffusionDet achieves 45.8 AP using a single sampling step and 300 random boxes, which significantly outperforms Faster RCNN [74] (40.2 AP), DETR [10] (42.0 AP) and on par with Sparse R-CNN [91] (45.0 AP).
its performance increases from 45.8 to 46.6 (+ 0.8 AP) on COCO while from 29.4 to 31.5 (+2.1 AP) on LVIS

limitations.summary: DiffusionDet relies on iterative denoising sampling, so like diffusion generative models it may suffer relatively slow sampling speed; the paper explores only the most fundamental DDIM strategy and leaves faster samplers to future work.
items: Inference requires iterative denoising sampling, which can be slower than single-pass detectors.
Only the basic DDIM diffusion strategy is used, without more advanced fast samplers.

evidence.quote: Similar to the Diffusion model employed in generation tasks, DiffusionDet may suffer from a relatively slow sampling speed.
we have utilized the most fundamental diffusion strategy, DDIM, in our pioneering exploration of using generation models for perception tasks.

futureDirections.direction: Explore more advanced, faster diffusion sampling strategies to remove the speed penalty of iterative refinement.
futureDirections.quote: We believe that a more advanced diffusion strategy could potentially address the issue of decreased speed performance of DiffusionDet, which we plan to explore in future work.

equations.name: Forward noising process
equations.expr: q(z_t | z_0) = N(z_t | sqrt(alpha_bar_t) * z_0, (1 - alpha_bar_t) * I)

deploymentClaims: Same trained network can be evaluated with arbitrary numbers of boxes and iteration steps without retraining

evidence.quote: Our code is available at https://github.com/ ShoufaChen/DiffusionDet.
we can train DiffusionDet with Ntrain random boxes while evaluating it with Neval random boxes, where the Neval is arbitrary and does not need to be equal to Ntrain
